steps.description: Execute a small-scale MLP capacity scan using PyTorch to test whether the function space for fitting the analytic constraint f(x)=sin(2πx)+0.5cos(4πx) is rigid. For each constraint count w∈{10,20,30,40,50}, scan hidden widths h∈{4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32}, train with Adam (lr=1e-3, max 10k epochs), and record the minimal width N_c(w) achieving zero violation (max absolute error ≤1e-3 on a held-out set of 100 points). Repeat with 3 random seeds (0,1,2) to verify stability. Plot N_c(w) vs w and report the finite N_c values and training/holdout errors.

Re-examine the hypothesis with a more challenging constraint function family (e.g., higher-frequency oscillatory or piecewise smooth functions) to test whether the observed boundedness of N_c(w) was an artifact of function simplicity. Run scans over w ∈ {10,20,30,40,50} and hidden widths h ∈ {4,8,...,32} using the same zero-violation criterion (max abs error ≤ 1e-3). Compare N_c(w) trends across function families to assess whether "rigidity" is robust or specific to simple analytic forms. Use 3 random seeds for stability.

plans.objective: [DIM: dynamics] **Gradient Flow Rigidity Hypothesis**. This hypothesis is the most testable and novel, as it connects the observed N_c(w) behavior to the dynamics of gradient flow, a well-studied area in optimization theory. It provides a clear numerical prediction (logarithmic growth of N_c(w)) that can be distinguished from the linear growth predicted by the measure hypothesis and the constant growth predicted by the structure hypothesis. Additionally, it aligns with the previous failure mode, where the system may have been incorrectly assuming a rigid solution space without considering the dynamic effects of gradient flow. The hypothesis can be tested by varying w and measuring N_c(w), and by analyzing the convergence rate of gradient flow as a function of w.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement a modular neural network training framework (using PyTorch) to simulate the TargetChain setup with tanh activation and Adam optimizer, implementing gradient flow dynamics and N_c(w) measurement for w ∈ {10,20,30,40,50} with 3-seed reproducibility. The code will generate validation data for comparing logarithmic (gradient flow) vs linear (measure) vs constant (structure) growth trends.
